claims.text: Traditional EAM reference potentials are unable to represent the many atomic configurations of an ab initio multicomponent-alloy liquid.
Replacing an EAM reference with an actively trained MLIP in TOR-TILD will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Replacing an EAM reference with an actively trained MLIP in TOR-TILD will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys with five or more principal elements.
The proposed MLIP should be trained on ab initio configurations sampled at melting and under slightly superheated liquid conditions.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
Disorder in the solid and atomic configurational complexity in the liquid are pronounced over approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
The flexible representation of many-body interactions in an MLIP can describe the atomic configurations and energy landscape more faithfully than a conventional EAM reference.
An MLIP can cover a larger relevant region of phase space than a conventional EAM reference.
An MLIP can be systematically trained to interpolate among diverse atomic environments in liquid and near-melting solid states.
Interpolation among diverse near-melting atomic environments improves overlap between reference and ab initio target configurations.
Improved reference–target overlap produces a smoother and shorter thermodynamic-integration path.
A smoother and shorter integration path reduces free-energy error caused by reference–target mismatch.
The MLIP intervention will improve integration-path mismatch by approximately a factor of 5–10 relative to conventional EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The MLIP intervention will reduce associated free-energy errors by approximately a factor of 5–10 relative to conventional EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The intervention may become less effective when compositional heterogeneity or dynamic fluctuations exceed the scope of the MLIP training data.
Rapid temperature variation may push the MLIP outside its validated regime.
Evidence from elemental and binary systems suggests that MLIPs can span diverse configurations better than EAM references.
